Field.Name: TargetCompID

This tag consists of 2 subcomponents: SubFirm ID and Session ID SubFirm ID is the left-most 3 characters. The next 3 characters represent Session ID. Example: EBR123 SubFirm ID: EBR Session ID: 123

Message.Name: Logon
Message.Description: Initiates connection from client side and approves connection if sent by the exchange. ResetSeqNumFlag allows clients to start a new session (reset session sequence numbers). The Heartbeat Interval is declared by the session initiator using the HeartBtInt field in the Logon message. The heartbeat interval timer should be reset after every message is transmitted (not just heartbeats). The HeartBtInt value should be agreed upon and specified by the Logon initiator (client) and echoed back by the Logon acceptor. The same HeartBtInt value is used by both sides, the Logon "initiator" and Logon "acceptor".

Field.Name: EncryptMethod
Field.Description: "0" - None. Security must be guaranteed on transport level

Field.Name: HeartBtInt
Field.Description: Heartbeat interval in seconds - Allowed values are between 5s and 60s, 30s is recommended

Field.Name: ResetSeqNumFlag
Field.Description: "N" - use previous sequences "Y" - reset sequences (start new session). If clients cannot recover the previous session they start new session with 1 and set this field to "Y". The flag should be used with caution especially during trading session as this might lead to business data loss

Field.Name: Username
Field.Description: Username

Field.Name: Password
Field.Description: Password

Message.Name: Logout
Message.Description: The message initiates or confirms termination of a FIX session.

Field.Description: Logout reason

Message.Name: ResendRequest
Message.Description: The message is used to recover an inbound session sequence if a message was missed.

Field.Name: BeginSeqNo
Field.Description: Sequence number of the first message in range to be resent

Field.Name: EndSeqNo
Field.Description: Sequence number of the last message in range to be resent

Message.Name: SequenceReset
Message.Description: The message may be used in two modes: Reset Mode forces counterparty to adjust inbound message sequence, GapFillFlag = "N" or omitted; Fill Gap Mode is used during retransmission of messages missed by a client. Administrative messages and rejected business messages are not to be retransmitted. Instead a Sequence Reset message with GapFillFlag = "Y" must be used.

Field.Name: GapFillFlag
Field.Description: "N" - sequence reset, the counterparty must adjust inbound sequence number. "Y" - indicates the message is used instead of administrative or business messages which are not to be resent

Field.Name: NewSeqNo
Field.Description: New adjusted sequence number

Message.Name: TestRequest
Message.Description: A Test message is useful for checking sequence numbers or verifying the communication line status. Connection participant received the message is required to reply with Heartbeat message referring to TestReqID of the initial message.

Field.Name: TestReqID
Field.Description: Identifier to be returned in resulting Heartbeat message

Message.Name: Heartbeat
Message.Description: Used for replying to the Test request as well as checking the status of communication.

Field.Name: TestReqID
Field.Description: Identifier to be returned in resulting Heartbeat message

Message.Name: Reject
Message.Description: Issued by a party if an incoming FIX message is unsupported or not properly formed. Rejected messages must not be resent if a Resend Request is received; instead a SequenceReset with GapFillFlag = "Y" is expected.

Field.Name: Text

CTI 1: Transactions initiated and executed by an individual member for his/her own account, for an account he/she controls, or for an account in which he/she has ownership or financial interest.
CTI 2: Transactions executed for the proprietary account of a clearing member or non-clearing member firm.

CTI 3: Transactions where an individual member or authorized trader executes for the personal account of another individual member, for an account the other individual member controls or for an account in which the other individual member has ownership or financial interest.
CTI 4: Any transaction not meeting the definition of CTI 1, 2 or 3. (These should be non-member customer transactions).
